summary.text: 期 means a period, date, or time limit. In the 月-bearing form, 月 contributes a time-related meaning and 其 supplies the sound. Bronze forms are also reported with 日; the original motivation and sequence of these forms are unsettled.

formation.text: The 月-bearing form is phonosemantic: 月 contributes a time-related meaning and 其 supplies the sound. Shuowen glosses 期 as 會, “meeting,” and gives this analysis. Bronze forms are also reported with 日 and 其; a lunar-cycle explanation is not established as the original motivation.

components.text: In the 月-bearing form, 月 contributes a time-related meaning. Bronze forms are also reported with 日 in this role; the evidence does not settle the original motivation.
其 is identified as the sound element in 期. Although 其 itself is interpreted as an early picture of a winnowing basket, that picture does not contribute to this compound’s meaning.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin pair and historical comparisons are compatible with a sound relationship but do not independently establish 其’s role in this graph.

sound.text: Both characters are recorded as gi in the Middle Chinese column of the supplied table.
The Old Chinese forms are similar but distinct: *gə for 其 and *[g](r)ə for 期.
Modern Mandarin readings are qí for 其 and qī for 期.

history.text: Bronze forms of 期 are reported with either 日 or 月 alongside 其. Shuowen calls 𣅆, written with 日 and 丌, an ancient form. Another study places the graph 期 in mid-to-late Spring-and-Autumn materials and treats 日-based spellings as earlier graphs for the word. These accounts do not settle the dating or sequence of the forms.

A bronze inscription uses the separate graph 其 to write the word 期. This proposed whole-graph borrowing reuses a sign for a different word because the spoken forms were thought to sound alike; the basket’s ancient spoken name and the sound match are not independently confirmed here.
朞 is documented as a variant of 期 with a rearranged graphic structure, not as a demonstrated ancestor. The evidence does not support a sequence 㫷 → 朞 → 期.

uncertainties.text: The precise dating of particular early forms and the priority of the attested meanings remain unsettled; the original motivation is not established as a lunar cycle.

senses.text: Shuowen glosses 期 as 會, “meeting”; this dictionary gloss does not establish it as the earliest meaning.

senses.period: Spring-and-Autumn bronze inscriptions; individual dating and priority unresolved
senses.text: A bronze inscription is interpreted as using 期 for a calendrical interval, though this example does not show that this use preceded other early meanings.

senses.period: Spring-and-Autumn bronze inscriptions; individual dating and priority unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples are reported for a limit or deadline. A modern study also cites transmitted poetry for appointed-time uses, though it identifies no dated manuscript witness.

senses.gloss: period of time, date, or time limit
senses.text: Current definitions include a period of time, a date, and a time limit.

limitations.text: The attested contexts do not establish a chronological semantic chain among meeting, calendrical interval, and limit or appointed time.
The evidence does not establish that present meanings developed from a lunar-cycle sense.

components.text: 月 contributes a time-related meaning in one reported form; bronze forms also show 日 in this role.
其 supplies the sound element. Historical comparisons support a sound relationship, though they do not alone prove its role here.
